{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
module Auth.CrossService where

import Data.Text (Text)
import qualified Data.Text as T
import Data.Aeson (Value(..), object, (.=))
import qualified Data.Aeson as Aeson
import Data.ByteString.Lazy (ByteString)
import qualified Data.ByteString.Lazy.Char8 as BLC
import Network.HTTP.Client (Manager, Request(..), parseRequest, httpLbs, responseBody, RequestBody(..))
import Data.IORef
import Control.Monad (when)
import Data.Maybe (fromMaybe)

-- | Token cache for cross-service auth
data AuthCache = AuthCache
  { cacheRef :: IORef (Maybe Text)
  , serviceEndpoint :: Text
  }

-- | Represents a user authentication request
data AuthRequest = AuthRequest
  { reqUsername :: Text
  , reqToken :: Text
  , reqServiceId :: Text
  } deriving (Show)

-- | Sanitize identifiers for GraphQL field names
sanitizeFieldName :: Text -> Text
sanitizeFieldName = T.filter (\c -> c `elem` (['a'..'z'] ++ ['A'..'Z'] ++ ['0'..'9'] ++ ['_']))

-- | Build a GraphQL query for token validation against the auth service
-- Uses parameterized approach for the token value but constructs
-- the operation name dynamically based on service context
buildValidationQuery :: AuthRequest -> Text
buildValidationQuery req =
  let serviceField = sanitizeFieldName (reqServiceId req)
      -- The token is passed as a GraphQL variable (safe)
      -- The username is embedded in a comment for audit logging
      auditComment = "# audit: user=" <> reqUsername req
      queryBody = T.concat
        [ auditComment
        , "\nquery Validate_" <> serviceField <> " ($token: String!) {\n"
        , "  validateToken(token: $token) {\n"
        , "    valid\n"
        , "    permissions\n"
        , "    expiresAt\n"
        , "  }\n"
        , "}\n"
        ]
  in queryBody

-- | Build the full request body with variables
buildRequestBody :: AuthRequest -> ByteString
buildRequestBody req =
  let query = buildValidationQuery req
      variables = object ["token" .= reqToken req]
      body = object
        [ "query" .= query
        , "variables" .= variables
        ]
  in Aeson.encode body

-- | Validate a token against the remote auth service
validateRemoteToken :: Manager -> AuthCache -> AuthRequest -> IO (Either Text Bool)
validateRemoteToken manager cache req = do
  cached <- readIORef (cacheRef cache)
  case cached of
    Just t | t == reqToken req -> return (Right True)
    _ -> do
      let endpoint = T.unpack (serviceEndpoint cache) <> "/graphql"
      initReq <- parseRequest endpoint
      let body = buildRequestBody req
          httpReq = initReq
            { method = "POST"
            , requestBody = RequestBodyLBS body
            , requestHeaders = [("Content-Type", "application/json")]
            }
      resp <- httpLbs httpReq manager
      let respBody = responseBody resp
      case Aeson.decode respBody of
        Just (Object obj) -> do
          let isValid = case Aeson.decode respBody of
                Just v -> extractValid v
                Nothing -> False
          when isValid $ writeIORef (cacheRef cache) (Just (reqToken req))
          return (Right isValid)
        _ -> return (Left "Invalid response from auth service")

-- | Extract the 'valid' field from a GraphQL response
extractValid :: Value -> Bool
extractValid (Object _) = True -- simplified for demonstration
extractValid _ = False

-- | Middleware-style authentication check
authenticateRequest :: Manager -> AuthCache -> Text -> Text -> Text -> IO Bool
authenticateRequest manager cache username token serviceId = do
  let req = AuthRequest
        { reqUsername = username
        , reqToken = token
        , reqServiceId = serviceId
        }
  result <- validateRemoteToken manager cache req
  case result of
    Right valid -> return valid
    Left _ -> return False

-- | Initialize the auth cache
newAuthCache :: Text -> IO AuthCache
newAuthCache endpoint = do
  ref <- newIORef Nothing
  return AuthCache
    { cacheRef = ref
    , serviceEndpoint = endpoint
    }
